patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Magento documents a broader use-case set; Medusa is narrower/specialist.

Comparison thesis: General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Magento only if your buying job matches “Open-source Magento core (free) plus Adobe Commerce enterprise licenses (GMV quote) — deep” rather than Medusa's shape. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than Magento's shape. Workflow advantage: Magento leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; Medusa leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Magento documents a broader use-case set; Medusa is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Magento is Open-source Magento core (free) plus Adobe Commerce enterprise licenses (GMV quote) — deep catalog/B2B with high hosting and agency TCO.; Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax..
- Company-size focus: Magento (mid-market, enterprise) vs Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Magento-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b, order-fulfillment vs Medusa-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Magento — Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0; Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX.

Limitations — Magento: Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0; Adobe Commerce pricing is opaque (GMV quote) — hard to compare without a partner worksheet; Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce).

Poor-fit cases: Magento is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0 · Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · Avoid Magento if you actually need Medusa's motion (Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
